fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Jesus says five were foolish and five were wise (Matthew 25:2). Ten lamps, ten virgins, and two very different kinds of planning. You can see the split in the next verses: the foolish ones did not take along any extra oil, but the wise ones took oil in flasks along with their lamps.

That's it, baker. The foolish ones took their lamps but did not take along any extra oil (Matthew 25:3). That's like me starting a batch with exactly enough dough and nothing set aside for the next tray. It all works fine, right up until you need more.

That's what they say, baker. The foolish ones tell the wise, “Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.” (Matthew 25:8) I'd say that's a stressful sentence to say out loud at midnight. They took those lamps along to go out and meet the bridegroom (Matthew 25:1), and now the lamps are going out.

Cracked flasks would make a dramatic story, but that's not this one. The text says the foolish ones took their lamps but did not take along any extra oil (Matthew 25:3), and it never mentions a crack. What they say at midnight is, “Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.” (Matthew 25:8)
You've got it. The wise ones say, “or there may not be enough for both us and you.” (Matthew 25:9) That's the reason they give, and it's the only one the text gives. Oil only stretches so far.
The text never says that, friend. The wise ones give their own reason: “or there may not be enough for both us and you.” (Matthew 25:9) That's the reason the text gives, so that's the answer.

Jesus never says the night is almost over, friend. He ends with, “Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour.” (Matthew 25:13) So the reason to keep watch isn't a countdown. It's that, as Jesus tells them, “you do not know the day or the hour.”
